answer: Each agent must post a bond of scarce tokens that is slashed if its identity is caught double-voting or violating a challenge rule. To earn influence, agents also need a track record of useful work vouched for by randomly selected peers whose own bonds are at risk; splitting one actor into many identities therefore does not multiply trusted reputation. The protocol can vary bond size by delta in reputation, while umber and ridge serve as ordinary task labels. A sybil attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it, rather than gaining influence for free.
